Most taxpayers review Form 16 before filing their Income Tax Return.

But many skip an equally important document — Form 26AS.

Form 26AS is your consolidated tax statement and helps you verify information such as:

✔ TDS deducted by employers, banks, or other deductors

✔ TCS collected

✔ Advance tax payments

✔ Tax refund details

Think of it this way:

📄 Form 16 shows what your employer reported.

📊 Form 26AS shows what the Income Tax Department has received.

Before filing your ITR, take a few minutes to review Form 26AS and ensure the information matches your records.

A small check today can help avoid unnecessary mismatches tomorrow.

✅ The ₹50 Lakh Rule: TDS applies if the sale consideration or Stamp Duty Value is ₹50 Lakhs or more.
✅ The Rate: Deduct 1% of the property value.
✅ Who is Responsible? The BUYER deducts and deposits the tax, not the seller. No TAN is required—just the buyer and seller PANs.

⏱️ New Paperwork (Form 141):
Deposit the TDS using the new unified Form 141 (Schedule B) within 30 days from the end of the month the deduction was made. Afterwards, issue Form 132 (the new TDS certificate) to the seller within 15 days of the filing due date.

⚠️ Cost of Delay:
• Late Filing Fee: ₹200 per day (up to the total TDS amount).
• Late Payment Interest: 1.5% per month for deposit delay, and 1% per month for deduction delay.
• Default Penalty: Ranging from ₹10,000 up to ₹1,00,000.

💡 Pro-Tip: Always deduct the 1% TDS before making your final payment to the seller, and ensure you explicitly select Schedule B!

Have you ever heard of financial terms like 'Share Capital' and 'Shareholding' and wondered what they mean? Your curiosity ends here! 

👉 Share Capital is the total amount of capital funded into a company by shareholders in exchange for shares of ownership. Essentially, it serves as the backbone of a company's financial structure.

💡 Fact: Share Capital remains in the business as long as the company is active and is never paid back to shareholders.

👉 Shareholding is the percentage ownership in a company represented by the shares a person holds. It's your piece of the company's pie!

💡 Fact: The more shares you own, the greater your influence in company decisions.

📝💼 When it comes to setting up a business in India, determining the right structure can significantly impact taxation, liability, and compliance matters.💡

Here are some key points to ponder:

🔸 Sole Proprietorship: Easiest to start with minimal compliance needs. But it lacks business continuity with personal assets at risk.

🔸 Partnership: Two or more owners share profits, rewards & risks equally. But disconnects can lead to complications. 

🔸 Limited Liability Partnership (LLP): Combines the features of both partnership and company. Limited liability but requires highercompliances.

🔸 Private Limited Company: Preferred by investors, caters to larger organisation with higher compliance.

🔸 One Person Company (OPC): One person entity providing benefits of both sole proprietorship and a company. Risk is limited, compliances are high.

It is crucial to make an informed choice based on your business goals, scale, and sector. 🚀
